follow_up_issue.title: Replace the bool aligned / bool dma template flags of view and const_view with enum types
follow_up_issue.body_markdown:
## Why

`view` and `const_view` take two boolean template parameters, `aligned` and `dma` (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:17-18, views.hpp:23-24, h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:18-21). Call sites spell them as bare `true, false` (82 lines in 20 files at PR #4557 head c73e7fb2f9, for example h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1960 `view<bf16, true, false, seq<head_size>>`). Two flags of the same type can be swapped without a compile error. PR #4557 added the named constants `VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE` and `VIEW_DMA_FALSE` (h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp:24-25) on its own 31 lines. The maintainer review of that PR asked for enum types instead and marked it as a follow-up: https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4557#discussion_r4133613638

## What

Make the two flags proper enum types so that swapped arguments and bare literals fail to compile:

```cpp
// h/tron/tensor/views.hpp (next to the existing dma comment)
enum class view_alignment : uint8_t { unaligned, aligned };
enum class view_memory : uint8_t { host, dma };

template <typename T,
    view_alignment aligned,
    view_memory dma,
    typename Dim,
    typename Stride = row_major<Dim>>
struct view;
```

A call site then reads `view<bf16, view_alignment::aligned, view_memory::host, seq<head_size>, sseq<1>>{dest}` (today: h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2762).

The repo already uses enum class template parameters: `rope_scaling` / `rope_layout` (h/tron/kernels/rope.hpp:95, :275) and `moe_scale_mode` (h/tron/models/mixture_of_experts.hpp:275).

## Scope (counts at c73e7fb2f9)

- Parameter declarations that must change type: view.hpp 17 lines, views.hpp 15, slice.hpp 6, tensor.hpp 7 (`dma1`/`dma2` included), expr.hpp 2, dotter.hpp 29 (its `template <typename U, bool dma>` members deduce from view types).
- Static members and their readers: `static constexpr bool dma` in tensor.hpp:35, :254, itensor.hpp:26, dmatensor.hpp:38, :173; readers tensor.hpp:415-416 (`Activation::dma`, `Result::dma`) and model.hpp:2831 (`v_buffer_t::dma`); `constexpr bool is_dma` in mixture_of_experts.hpp:535 and feed_forward.hpp:489.
- Consumers that branch on `aligned`: view.hpp:157-158 forwards it to `chunky<T, aligned>` and `readable_in_chunks<T, aligned>`; slice.hpp:56, :93 and simd/aligned.hpp:14-66 use `if constexpr (aligned)`. Either convert at the view boundary (`aligned == view_alignment::aligned`) and leave the SIMD-level `bool aligned` in wide.hpp (46 lines), chunky.hpp, clamp.hpp, simd/aligned.hpp as is, or convert those too. Decide in the PR.
- Call sites: 82 lines passing bare `true`/`false` in 20 files, plus the 31 lines in 9 files that use `VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE` / `VIEW_DMA_FALSE` (delete the two constants), plus the aliases PR #4697 adds (`bool Dma = VIEW_DMA_FALSE`).
- `gptq_view<bool permuted, ...>` in safetensors.hpp is a different flag; leave it.

## Ordering

Land after #4557 and #4697. Coordinate with any open PR that spells view flags (for example #4424).

## Acceptance

- No `bool aligned` / `bool dma` parameter remains on `view`, `const_view`, `views`, `const_views`, `lambda_views`, `id_views`, `array_views`, `slice`, `dotter`, `t_launch_matmul`.
- `view<bf16, true, false, ...>` and a swapped `view<bf16, view_memory::host, view_alignment::aligned, ...>` fail to compile (add a compile-time test next to h/tron/tensor/array_like.hpp:24-30 static_asserts).
- Existing tests pass (t_fp32, t_attention, t_llama_unit, t_heterogeneous_scheduler, t_amx_numerics, t_amx_dispatch_dtype).
- The generated code is unchanged apart from symbol names: compare the defined-symbol counts of t_llama_unit and t_amx_numerics before and after, as commit 5051264d80 did.

Sketch (10 lines, follows the guide: enumerators are named values, no literals):
```cpp
enum class view_alignment : uint8_t { unaligned, aligned };
enum class view_memory : uint8_t { host, dma };
template <typename T, view_alignment aligned, view_memory dma, typename Dim, typename Stride = row_major<Dim>>
struct view;
// inside view.hpp where chunky is called:
static constexpr bool CHUNK_ALIGNED = aligned == view_alignment::aligned;
if constexpr (s0 == 1 && readable_in_chunks<T, CHUNK_ALIGNED>) { return chunky<T, CHUNK_ALIGNED>::get(data, i); }
// tensor.hpp:35 becomes
static constexpr view_memory dma = view_memory::host;
```

Words used here: view / const_view (tron's fixed-shape tensor view types in h/tron/tensor/view.hpp), aligned flag (the data pointer is 64-byte aligned so chunked SIMD loads are allowed), dma flag (the memory is DMA-safe for the FPGA), NTTP (non-type template parameter), scoped enum (enum class; no implicit conversion to int or bool).

1. Follow-up issue, as you suggested: the constants stay until the follow-up converts the parameters repo-wide. Issue: (link).
2. In this PR: define `enum class view_alignment { unaligned, aligned }` and `enum class view_memory { host, dma }` in `kv_cache_fwd.hpp`, plus alias templates `typed_view` / `typed_const_view` that map them onto the existing bool parameters. Main stays untouched, every resulting type is identical to today's, swapped or bare-literal arguments fail to compile, and the two constants go away. The follow-up then moves the enums into `views.hpp`. The four `bool Dma = VIEW_DMA_FALSE` heads in #4697 would become `view_memory memory = view_memory::host`.

items.target: fact (insufficient-data): VNNI = Vector Neural Network Instructions, the AVX-512/AMX dot-product family whose B operand is pair-interleaved; VDPBF16PS and TDPBF16PS consume that layout
items.why: The expansion and the pair-interleaved B operand hold (repo precedent). The grouping is loose: VDPBF16PS is not a VNNI instruction in the compiler's own naming. GCC keeps _mm512_dpbf16_ps in avx512bf16intrin.h under `#pragma GCC target("avx512bf16")`, while avx512vnniintrin.h (`avx512vnni`) has no bf16 dot product; the CPU also reports avx512_vnni and avx512_bf16 as separate flags. "VNNI layout" is the name of the operand layout, borrowed from the instruction family that introduced it. This matters for the wording of the option-B hunk (next item).
items.correction: "VNNI (Vector Neural Network Instructions) is Intel's name for a dot-product instruction family; 'VNNI layout' names their pair-interleaved B operand. VDPBF16PS (AVX512_BF16) and TDPBF16PS (AMX-BF16) consume the same layout but belong to other extensions."

reviewer_claims.claim: (i) "The C++ spec states that an implicitly-created object's (that is, one not introduced by a new expression) lifetime must begin in an operator new."
reviewer_claims.evidence: operator new / operator new[] is one item on the list, not the only one. N4950 [intro.object]/13 names operator new, operator new[], and starting the lifetime of an unsigned char or std::byte array; its note adds std::malloc and relatives ([c.malloc]/4), memcpy/memmove ([cstring.syn]/3), bit_cast ([bit.cast]/2) and std::start_lifetime_as ([obj.lifetime]/3). The Note's point is narrower: dma_allocate_aligned is on none of these lists (h/system/memory.hpp:146 declares it as an ordinary extern function), so the PR routes the allocation through a function named operator new[] (memory.hpp:185-189, :369-370).

reviewer_claims.claim: (ii) "the previous implementation was strictly-speaking incorrect: it allocated storage but failed to actually begin the lifetime of the object residing in that storage."
reviewer_claims.evidence: On main, try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite called dma_allocate_aligned directly (main memory.hpp:331) and the accessors cast the byte pointer with a plain reinterpret_cast (main kv_cache.hpp:1533, :1542, :1578). Neither step creates an object ([intro.object]/10, /13), and a member access through the resulting pointer is undefined behaviour ([basic.life]/6). The first PR commit b951ba9b4c fixed it with a placement-new second pass (construct_kv_blocks, :1472-1495); commit 39a6899446 replaced that pass with the operator new[] wrapper plus std::launder in the accessors (HEAD kv_cache.hpp:1565, :1574, :1614).

reviewer_claims.claim: (iii) "Previously this was perhaps okay since the storage held POD, but now it contains a v_vnni_tensor, requiring that we be a bit more careful."
reviewer_claims.evidence: The rule is the same before and after. Old kv_block was an aggregate of bf16s arrays (main kv_cache.hpp:2449-2459); it was an implicit-lifetime type, and the old allocation still created no object of it, so the old code was not okay under the standard (and bf16s = __m256i, types.hpp:26, is not an ISO type at all). New kv_block is still an aggregate with no user-provided destructor ([class.prop]/9 first branch; HEAD kv_cache.hpp:2445-2459), and v_vnni_tensor has a trivial implicit default constructor and a trivial destructor ([class.prop]/9 second branch; v_vnni.hpp:246-269), pinned by static_assert at kv_cache.hpp:2455-2458, :1554-1557, :1597-1600 and STATIC_REQUIRE at t_llama_unit.cpp:450-452, :459-460. So v_vnni_tensor needs no extra care; what changed is that the PR makes the allocation satisfy the rule that both versions needed. The one true part: v_vnni_tensor has a private member, so it is not an aggregate, and the second branch of [class.prop]/9 is what covers it; the static_asserts exist to keep that true.

plain_words_table.says: In C++, a call of any function named operator new[] creates objects in the memory it returns ([intro.object]).
plain_words_table.plain: C++ has a rule: when a program calls any function whose name is operator new[] (our wrapper counts, because that is its name), the memory that call returns is treated as already holding objects. No constructor runs. The rule is N4950 [intro.object]/13.

plain_words_table.says: The objects created are the ones the program goes on to use.
plain_words_table.plain: The rule does not say which objects appear. It says: whichever set of objects makes the later code well defined is the set that was created ([intro.object]/10). For the KV book that set is the kv_block arrays the accessors read.
The rule works only for types that C++ lets an allocation create without a constructor call. The standard calls these implicit-lifetime types ([basic.types.general]/9, [class.prop]/9).

plain_words_table.says: for example scalars, arrays, and classes with a trivial constructor and destructor.
plain_words_table.plain: Numbers and pointers, arrays of anything on this list, and classes whose default constructor and destructor do nothing (kv_block, v_vnni_tensor, bf16 all qualify; the static_asserts at kv_cache.hpp:2455-2458 and :1554-1557 keep it so).

plain_words_table.says: dma_allocate_aligned is an ordinary function, so its memory holds no objects.
plain_words_table.plain: dma_allocate_aligned is not named operator new, is not malloc, is not memcpy. So the rule does not apply to it: the bytes it returns are just bytes, and no kv_block exists in them, whatever we cast the pointer to.

plain_words_table.says: So try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite gets its memory through the wrapper below.
plain_words_table.plain: That is why the fallible DMA factory (the only allocator the KV book uses, kv_cache.hpp:1289, :1424, :1434) calls the operator new[] wrapper (memory.hpp:369-370) instead of dma_allocate_aligned: the call itself creates the kv_blocks.

The wrapper only forwards the request to dma_allocate_aligned (memory.hpp:188). Object creation here is a rule about what the program may assume, not a memory write. The memory stays uninitialized, which is what "for_overwrite" promises.

plain_words_table.says: Call the wrapper directly, never from a new-expression.
plain_words_table.plain: Write ::operator new[](bytes, dma_allocation, alignment). Do not write new (dma_allocation, alignment) T[n].

plain_words_table.says: An array new-expression may ask for extra bytes ([expr.new]), and dma_deallocate would not free them.
plain_words_table.plain: The new T[n] form may request more than n * sizeof(T) bytes and hand back a pointer past the start of the block ([expr.new]/16, /20). dma_deallocate expects the exact block start and size, so that form would leak or corrupt.

plain_words_table.says: No test fails if a caller goes back to calling dma_allocate_aligned directly.
plain_words_table.plain: Warning: the test suite cannot catch a regression to the old form.

plain_words_table.says: The unit-test allocator (aligned_alloc in src/pos/fake.cpp) creates objects by itself, so the tests behave the same either way.
plain_words_table.plain: Because in unit tests dma_allocate_aligned is aligned_alloc (fake.cpp:354), which is on the standard's list of object-creating functions ([c.malloc]/4). Only production (the real DMA allocator) lacks the rule.

Your second reading is right on the main point: on main, `try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite` called `dma_allocate_aligned` directly and the accessors cast the bytes with a plain `reinterpret_cast`, so no `kv_block` ever started its lifetime. A member access through such a pointer is undefined behaviour ([basic.life]/6), and nothing diagnoses it.

Two small corrections, so the Note does not mislead the next reader:

- `operator new` is one item on the list, not the only one. N4950 [intro.object]/13 and its note also list `malloc` and relatives, `memcpy`/`memmove`, `bit_cast`, and starting the lifetime of a `std::byte` array. The point of the Note is that `dma_allocate_aligned` is on none of these lists, so I route the allocation through a function named `operator new[]`.
- `v_vnni_tensor` does not need more care than the old `kv_block`. Both are implicit-lifetime types ([class.prop]/9): the old `kv_block` was an aggregate of arrays, the new one still is, and `v_vnni_tensor` has a trivial implicit default constructor and a trivial destructor. The `static_assert` at kv_cache.hpp:2455-2458 (and the ones in the accessors at :1554 and :1597) keep that true. So the rule was the same before and after; what changed is that the allocation now satisfies it.

I have reworded the Note in plain words: what the KV book does, what an implicit-lifetime type is, the full list of operations that create such objects, why `dma_allocate_aligned` is not one of them, what goes wrong without the wrapper, and why the unit tests cannot tell the difference (`aligned_alloc` is on the list, [c.malloc]/4). Same title, same three paragraphs of facts. Does the new text read clearly to you?

follow_up_issue.title: make_unique_dma and make_unique_dma_for_overwrite allocate through dma_allocate_aligned and create no objects for trivially constructible element types
follow_up_issue.body_markdown:
## Short version

PR #4557 routes `try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite` through a function named `operator new[]`, so its memory holds the objects the caller reads (Note [DMA allocation creates objects], h/system/memory.hpp). The three sibling factories still call `dma_allocate_aligned` directly. For trivially constructible element types they run no placement new, so in strict C++ their memory holds no objects.

## Where

At PR #4557 head c73e7fb2f9, h/system/memory.hpp:

- `make_unique_dma<T>` (:239-241): `dma_allocate_aligned` then `std::memset` for trivially constructible `T`.
- `make_unique_dma<T[]>` (:254-257): same, with `std::memset` over the array.
- `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T>` (:274-275): `dma_allocate_aligned`, placement new only when `T` is not trivially constructible.
- `make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<T[]>` (:286-289): same for arrays.

`std::memset` is not one of the operations that implicitly create objects (N4950 [intro.object]/13 and its note list `operator new`/`operator new[]`, `malloc` and relatives [c.malloc], `memcpy`/`memmove` [cstring.syn], `bit_cast` [bit.cast], `start_lifetime_as` [obj.lifetime]). A member access on the result is undefined behaviour ([basic.life]/6).

## Why it matters

Today's compilers do not diagnose this, and the unit-test allocator (`aligned_alloc` in src/pos/fake.cpp:354) creates objects by itself ([c.malloc]/4), so no test can show it. The production DMA allocator gives no such guarantee. This is the same class of gap that the maintainer review of PR #4557 (comment 4133869073) called strictly incorrect for the KV book.

## Proposed fix

Route all four factories through the tagged `operator new[]` wrapper added by PR #4557 (or a matching `operator new` for the single-object forms). The wrapper writes no bytes, so behaviour and performance stay the same. Keep the `TRON_ASSERT` on null in the asserting forms.

## Out of scope

The non-ISO reads tracked in #4588 (`scaled_v_expr`, `fill_storage_slot`, the 8-lane V accessors) are a separate gap.

Label: Tech Debt.

Row 1 (main 996f58ec82): dma_allocate_aligned -> bytes -> reinterpret_cast<kv_block_t*> -> member access, with the last arrow marked \"no object here ([basic.life]/6)\". Row 2 (HEAD c73e7fb2f9): ::operator new[](bytes, dma_allocation, alignment) -> bytes that now hold uint8_t[] + nested kv_block[] ([intro.object]/13) -> std::launder(reinterpret_cast<kv_block_t*>) -> member access, all arrows solid. Side box: \"implicit-lifetime? old kv_block: aggregate of bf16s arrays = yes; new kv_block: aggregate = yes; v_vnni_tensor: trivial ctor + trivial dtor = yes (static_assert kv_cache.hpp:2455-2458)\". Table for the page: object-creating operations vs. what tron uses (operator new[] wrapper: yes, production; aligned_alloc: yes, unit tests only via fake.cpp:354; dma_allocate_aligned: no; memset in make_unique_dma: no). Plain-words term list for the page: implicit-lifetime type (a type C++ lets an allocation create without a constructor call); implicit object creation (the rule that certain calls make objects exist in the memory they return); std::launder (turns an address into a pointer to the object that lives there); new-expression (the `new T[n]` syntax, as opposed to a direct call of a function named operator new[]); aggregate (a class with only public members and no user-written constructors); DMA (direct memory access: the FPGA-reachable memory pool); KV book (the KV cache's arena manager, class book in kv_cache.hpp).

Thanks for reading it twice. Your second reading is right on the main point: on main, `try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite` called `dma_allocate_aligned` directly and the accessors cast the bytes with a plain `reinterpret_cast`, so no `kv_block` ever started its lifetime. A member access through such a pointer is undefined behaviour ([basic.life]/6).

Two small corrections, so the Note does not mislead the next reader:

- `operator new` is one item on the list, not the only one. N4950 [intro.object]/13 also names starting the lifetime of an `unsigned char` or `std::byte` array, and its note adds `malloc` and relatives, `memcpy`/`memmove`, `bit_cast` and `start_lifetime_as`. The point of the Note is that `dma_allocate_aligned` is on none of these lists, so I route the allocation through a function named `operator new[]`.
- `v_vnni_tensor` does not need more care than the old `kv_block`. Both are implicit-lifetime types ([class.prop]/9): the old `kv_block` was an aggregate of arrays, the new one still is, and `v_vnni_tensor` has a trivial implicit default constructor and a trivial destructor. The `static_assert` at kv_cache.hpp:2455-2458 (and the ones in the accessors at :1554 and :1597) keep that true. So the rule was the same before and after; what changed is that the allocation now satisfies it.

I have reworded the Note in plain words: what the KV book does, what an implicit-lifetime type is, the full list of operations that create such objects, why `dma_allocate_aligned` is not one of them, what goes wrong without the wrapper, and why the unit tests cannot tell the difference (`aligned_alloc` is on the list, [c.malloc]/4). follow_up_issue.body_markdown:
## Short version

All three reads named in this issue are fixed by the maintainer's PR #4698 (commit 63df10cf90), now merged into the PR #4557 branch as commit <MERGE_COMMIT>. After that commit `h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp` holds no `reinterpret_cast` to or from `bf16`. Closing.

## What changed, per read

- Read 1, `scaled_v_expr`: the member `data` is now `const bf16*`. Every tile address is computed in `bf16` units and passed to the load intrinsic as a `bf16` pointer. Old and new load addresses were enumerated for head_size 64, 128, 256 and 512 in both lane widths. All are equal.
- Read 2, `fill_storage_slot`: `k` and `v` are filled as two separate arrays. No pointer crosses from `k` into `v`.
- Read 3, the 8-lane V accessors: `v` is declared `bf16 v[page_size * head_size]` in the 8-lane branch (the same form `k` took in c73e7fb2f9). `page::v`, `page::v_ptr`, `copy_storage_slot` and `page::scaled_v` build their views without a cast.

## Evidence

- PR #4698 CI: 20 of 20 checks pass (Build Tron, Test, Test host, Test FPGA, Benchmark, Lint).
- The PR #4698 commit message: AVX-512 `t_llama_unit` passed all 44 cases (252720 assertions).

## Still open, not tracked here

- The 8-lane (AVX2) hunks are not compiled or run by any CI job. The 8-lane `t_llama_unit` build has 131 errors before this change (see the section "State of the 8-lane build" above). The change cannot make that build worse in `kv_cache.hpp`, and it was not verified there.
- The other "outside ISO C++" items that this issue lists as not in scope (EAGLE x_data casts, intrinsic and AMX tile loads, the discarded placement new in token_tree.hpp) keep no tracker.

open_for_jhan: Merge PR #4698 as a merge commit, or cherry-pick 63df10cf90 onto jhan-kv-typed-tensors? (Both leave the PR #4557 head one commit past c73e7fb2f9; a cherry-pick lets you rewrite the message; a merge keeps #4698 auto-closing.)

Apply your named-value rule to the merged code or list the exception? The reviewer's diff has bare literals: `2 * chunk_size * 0` .. `* 15` (the 2 = bf16 values per 32-bit lane, the 0-15 = register index matching t0-t15), `part * 8 * chunk_size` and `part * 8` (8 registers per pass; `part * 8` is pre-existing on main), `load(0)` .. `load(7)`.

Run t_llama_unit on 3bda after the merge for our own record? The reviewer's commit message reports 44 cases / 252720 assertions on AVX-512; the task rules forbade touching 3bda here, so no run was made.
Close #4588 after the merge, or keep it open for the 8-lane compile gap? The recommendation above closes it and states the 8-lane gap in the closing comment.

items.why: Recomputed by hand in bytes. 16-lane old: data is bf16s* (32 B units), tile = data + i*(head_size/16) cast to bf16x32* (64 B) + chunk_offset, register n at +64n B -> byte offset 2*i*head_size + 64*chunk_offset + 64n. 16-lane new: bf16 units (2 B), data + i*head_size + 32*chunk_offset + 32n -> the same bytes. 8-lane old: bf16s = 16 B units, data + i*(head_size/8) + part*8 + n -> 2*i*head_size + 128*part + 16n B. 8-lane new: data + i*head_size + 64*part + 8n in 2 B units -> the same bytes. Alignment stays 64 B in the 16-lane loop because i is even and head_size >= 64.

follow_up_issue.title: Packed K (PR 4424 rebase): decide whether the packed-K types get a logical-row expression, matching the packed-V decision on PR 4557
follow_up_issue.body_markdown:
## Short version

PR 4557 gives the packed V plane a typed owner (`v_vnni_tensor`), a view (`v_vnni_view`) and a logical-row expression (`v_vnni_row`). The row type has no production caller; its one user is a host-tensor read in `t/t_llama_unit.cpp`. The maintainer asked on PR 4557 whether the row is worth its lines (review comment [4134076112](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4557#discussion_r4134076112)). The packed-K child (the rebase of PR 4424 onto PR 4557) should follow whatever PR 4557 settles on, and not add a `k_vnni_row` by symmetry alone.

## Words used here

- `expr`: the base class of tron's tensor expressions (`h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp`). A rank-2 `expr` supplies `operator[]` returning a rank-1 `expr`; a rank-1 `expr` supplies `chunk(i)` (16 fp32 values).
- logical row: one token's values in dimension order, as opposed to the interleaved pair rows of the packed layout.

## What to do

1. Read the outcome of the PR 4557 thread above (keep the row, or drop the row and the `expr` base and keep `at()` plus the bulk operations).
2. Apply the same shape to the packed K types when PR 4424 is rebased: either both planes are `expr`s with a logical-row type, or neither is.
3. If rows are dropped, remove the row-expression items from the design page (`design-new-tensor-type.html`, Q3 and the child section) so the child's plan and the code agree.

## Why it matters

A row expression for packed K would gather 16 values from 8 cache lines per chunk (design page, child section). That is an inspection read, not a production path. Keeping the two families the same shape keeps the 'who may compute a packed address' rule in `Note [Packed V layout]` short.

This issue closes with the PR 4424 rebase. It does not block PR 4557.

Counted: the row is 70 lines (`v_vnni_row` plus its comment, v_vnni.hpp 97-166), 85 with the two `operator[]` overloads on the view and the forward declarations.

Users today: none in production. - keep: nothing changes. The packed-K child then gets a matching `k_vnni_row`, also test-only.
- drop: remove `v_vnni_row`, the `expr` base of `v_vnni_view` and its `operator[]`; keep `at()` and the bulk operations. That is your sketch. Net -109 lines across 3 files, no production path touched. The diff is ready and passes a syntax compile at 16 lanes; a full build and test run at both lane counts is next.

Which do you prefer?

Title: Packed K: follow the PR 4557 decision on logical-row expressions

## Short version

PR 4557 gives the packed V plane (the V cache stored with two tokens interleaved per row) a typed owner `v_vnni_tensor`, a view `v_vnni_view` and a logical-row expression `v_vnni_row`. The row type has no production caller. Its one user is a test in `t/t_llama_unit.cpp` that builds a plain `tensor` from a packed view.

The maintainer noted on PR 4557 that the row adds about 100 lines without an obvious user, and that it does seem useful (review comment https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4557#discussion_r4134076112). The packed K change (the rebase of PR 4424, which stores K in the same interleaved layout, onto PR 4557) should follow whatever PR 4557 settles on. It should not add a `k_vnni_row` for symmetry only.

## Words used here

- `expr`: the base class of tron's tensor expressions (`h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp`).
- rank: the number of indices a tensor takes. A rank-2 `expr` supplies `operator[]`, which returns a rank-1 `expr`. A rank-1 `expr` supplies `chunk(i)`, which returns one SIMD register of fp32 (32-bit float) values: 16 values in the AVX-512 build, 8 in the AVX2 build.
- logical row: one token's values in dimension order, as opposed to the interleaved pair rows of the packed layout.

## What to do

1. Read the outcome of the PR 4557 thread linked above. The two outcomes are: keep the row, or drop the row and the `expr` base and keep `at()` plus the bulk operations.
2. Apply the same shape to the packed K types when PR 4424 is rebased. Either both planes are `expr`s with a logical-row type, or neither is.

## Why it matters

A row expression for packed K would gather 16 values from 8 cache lines per chunk. That is an inspection read, not a production path. Keeping the two families the same shape keeps the "who may compute a packed address" rule in the packed V layout Note (`h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp`) short.

This issue closes with the PR 4424 rebase. It does not block PR 4557.

(Internal note for jhan, not for the issue: if rows are dropped, record design page Q3 as rejected and apply its line 371 instruction to the child.)

follow_up_issue.title: Name the rank-2 KV plane views in kv_cache.hpp through the kv_cache_fwd.hpp aliases (optional cleanup)
follow_up_issue.body_markdown:
## Short version

PR #4697 (merged into the #4557 branch) gave the head-sized V transfer rows named aliases (`const_v_row_view`, `v_row_view`, `v_source_row`, `v_destination_row` in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp). Four rank-2 plane views in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp still spell `view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<page_size, head_size>>` out by hand. This issue asks whether they should use the `native_k_view` / `const_native_k_view` aliases of h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp, or a new plane alias.

## Sites (at commit 8bbbb7c82d)

- kv_cache.hpp:2391, `scaled_v_expr` constructor parameter (8-lane V plane, read-only)
- kv_cache.hpp:2469 and 2475, `kv_block::k_view()` writable and read-only
- kv_cache.hpp:2514, the 8-lane `scaled_v` call

## Open question

`native_k_view` spells its strides explicitly (`std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, Cols, 1>`). Whether that is the same type as the default-stride `view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>` decides if the K sites can switch without changing any signature. A `static_assert(std::is_same_v<...>)` in t_llama_unit settles it.

## Scope

Cosmetic. No behaviour change. Low priority; take it with the next edit of these lines.

Words used here: PR 4697 = the reviewer's pull request against jhan-kv-typed-tensors (the PR 4557 branch), head 8bbbb7c82d, base c73e7fb2f9. Row view = a one-dimensional view of head_size contiguous, 64-byte-aligned elements that page::set_v reads from and page::get_v writes to. Plane view = a two-dimensional view of a whole K or V plane (page_size x head_size). AMX-on tree = a build with -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON (the AMX software-attention kernels compiled); AMX-off tree = without it. 16-lane / 8-lane = TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 16 (AVX-512) / 8 (AVX2).

items.target: Follow-up issue 'Open question: whether native_k_view equals the default-stride view'
items.why: The analyst could have answered it from the code: view's default Stride is row_major<Dim> (views.hpp:26, 35), and row_major<seq<Rows, Cols>> expands to sseq<seq_stride<0>, seq_stride<1>> = the row-major strides (seq.hpp:376-394), i.e. std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, Cols, 1>, exactly what native_k_view spells (kv_cache_fwd.hpp:46-50). A default template argument names the same specialization, so the types are identical.

Title: Name the two-dimensional KV plane views in kv_cache.hpp through the kv_cache_fwd.hpp aliases (optional cleanup)

## Short version

PR #4697 (on the #4557 branch) gives the head-sized V transfer rows named aliases: `const_v_row_view`, `v_row_view`, `v_source_row` and `v_destination_row` in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp. Four two-dimensional plane views in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp still spell `view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<page_size, head_size>>` out by hand. This issue asks whether they should use the `native_k_view` / `const_native_k_view` aliases of h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp, or a new plane alias.

Words used here:
- plane view = a view over one whole K or V plane of a page (page_size rows by head_size columns)
- row view = a view over one head-sized row (the type the new aliases name)
- stride = the element distance between neighbouring rows or columns of a view
- 8-lane = the TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 8 (AVX2) build

## Sites (at commit 8bbbb7c82d, PR #4697)

- kv_cache.hpp:2391, the `scaled_v_expr` constructor parameter (8-lane V plane, read-only)
- kv_cache.hpp:2469 and 2475, `kv_block::k_view()` (writable and read-only)
- kv_cache.hpp:2514, the 8-lane `scaled_v` call

## Open question

`native_k_view` spells its strides explicitly, as `std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, Cols, 1>`. The K sites at kv_cache.hpp:2469 and 2475 use the default strides of `view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<page_size, head_size>>`. If the two are the same type, the K sites can switch without changing any signature. A `static_assert(std::is_same_v<...>)` in t_llama_unit settles it.

## Scope

Cosmetic. No behaviour change. Low priority. Take it with the next edit of these lines.
